bias_targets.methodology: Literature review and theoretical critique of existing computer vision benchmarks (e.g., tasks applying makeup to female faces or modifying women's clothing) and NLP models (e.g., reliance on binary gender assumptions and misgendering).
Critique of standard machine learning tasks, such as using Titanic passenger survival prediction, which implicitly relies on and normalizes wealth and social class proxies (fare purchased).
Literature review highlighting the limitations of current natural language processing research, which evaluates models predominantly on monolingual, English-language data.

Analysis of real-world historical AI failures, such as computer vision models misclassifying African Americans as 'gorillas', to illustrate the long-tail problem in dataset representation and evaluation.
